blocks.text: Éditions de La Martinière publish Lucien Hervé by Virginie Chardin . Of Hungarian origin, László Elkán (1907–2010), who took the pseudonym Lucien Hervé when he joined the Resistance in 1940, is often associated with the French humanist photography movement, which includes Robert Doisneau, Willy Ronis and Jean Dieuzaide. A painter with Communist sympathies, he took part in union actions and in reportages for the magazine Marianne before the war, and went on to photograph Paris and the Parisians after the Liberation. A decisive meeting with Father Marie-Alain Couturier, director of the journal L’Art Sacré and promoter of modern art, and then with the architect Le Corbusier in 1949, steered his work toward a singular path with no equivalent in France: an allegorical, aesthetic and artistic visual translation of the architectural thinking of the period, through an unrivaled interplay of variations between light and shadow.

This book, written by Virginie Chardin, sheds new light on the singular work of a photographer passionate about the spirit of forms and the creative power of light: alongside famous photographs, it presents little-known images and documents kept by his wife, Judith Hervé Elkán, and by various public and private institutions.
This fine book has been awarded the Bicentenary of Photography label by the French Ministry of Culture.

Virginie Chardin is an exhibition curator and author, a specialist in the history of photography. She has curated numerous exhibitions (Willy Ronis, Pierre de Fenoÿl, Sabine Weiss, Frank Horvat…). She has served as project officer at the Musée Nicéphore-Niépce, head of the awards at Les Rencontres d’Arles, delegate of the Mois de la Photo in Paris, patron of the Mentorat des Filles de la Photo, and nominator for the Niépce Prize. She is a member of the Association française des commissaires d’expositions (CEA) and of the International Council of Museums (ICOM). With Éditions de La Martinière, she has published Sabine Weiss (2016), Frank Horvat. 50-65 (2022) and Le Monde de Louis Stettner (2025).
Virginie Chardin : Lucien Hervé Les Éditions de La Martinière 17 x 24 cm 240 pages ISBN 9791040128311 €36 www.editionsdelamartiniere.fr
The exhibition “Lucien Hervé. Dialogue avec le soleil” can be seen at the Pavillon Populaire, the photography art space of the city of Montpellier, from December 9, 2026 to April 11, 2027.
